content: The American Diabetes Association emphasizes the importance of early evaluation and consistent monitoring of the efficacy and safety of metabolic surgery and related interventions. This is particularly critical because weight loss outcomes can vary significantly among individuals. If therapeutic targets are not achieved within three months, it may be beneficial to consider additional treatment options, including metabolic surgery. Metabolic surgery is a well-established and effective treatment for individuals with severe obesity, particularly those with a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m² or higher, in the context of diabetes management. These surgical procedures should be performed by interprofessional teams with expertise in both diabetes and obesity management, ideally within high-volume centers that specialize in such care. Following surgery, patients require comprehensive, lifelong medical care to ensure optimal outcomes. This care should include psychosocial and behavioral support to enhance long-term success and address the multifaceted needs of individuals undergoing this treatment.
